strings.name: Joy Buolamwini
strings.role: Computer scientist · Founder of the Algorithmic Justice League
strings.summary: Joy Buolamwini researches bias in AI systems and founded and leads the Algorithmic Justice League. She co-authored Gender Shades with Timnit Gebru, studied system performance after public audits with Inioluwa Deborah Raji, and uses writing and art to discuss algorithmic accountability. Findings concern specific tasks, datasets and historical versions, not all facial-recognition systems.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Birth date is not independently confirmed. Gender classification is distinguished from identity recognition, publication from testing dates, and podcast release from recording.
strings.influence.rationale: Researches facial-recognition bias and founded the Algorithmic Justice League, advancing debate on algorithmic fairness, accountability and public participation.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Earned a computer-science bachelor’s degree at Georgia Tech in 2012, then an Oxford education master’s and MIT master’s and doctorate.
strings.facts.f2.label: Research and expression
strings.facts.f2.value: Combines algorithmic auditing, public advocacy and art; author of Unmasking AI.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Auditing errors across intersecting groups
strings.highlights.h1.text: With Timnit Gebru, evaluated three commercial gender classifiers and found substantial performance differences across skin-tone and gender groups.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Bringing research into public debate
strings.highlights.h2.text: Uses the Algorithmic Justice League, books and art to encourage public discussion of AI’s effects and accountability.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Podcast conversation on AI and dignity
strings.timeline.t1.text: Mindful Mondays with Shudu releases a conversation about classification technology, power and human dignity; this is its release date, not a confirmed recording date.
strings.timeline.t2.title: LDF announces her board appointment
strings.timeline.t2.text: The Legal Defense Fund announces her election to its board, bringing digital-equity and AI-accountability experience to its governance; LDF and NAACP are separate organizations.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Digital civil rights award announced
strings.timeline.t3.text: AJL announces her 2024 NAACP–Archewell Foundation Digital Civil Rights Award for AI-equity advocacy; this is the announcement date.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Publishes Unmasking AI
strings.timeline.t4.text: Random House publishes her account of algorithmic harms and her research journey; the 2024 paperback is a later edition.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Earns MIT doctorate
strings.timeline.t5.text: The graduation roster and thesis catalog confirm a Media Arts and Sciences doctorate, examining algorithmic audits alongside artistic approaches that engage public perception.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Co-publishes Actionable Auditing
strings.timeline.t6.text: With Inioluwa Deborah Raji, studies commercial systems after public disclosure; the paper reports testing results as of August 2018.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Co-publishes Gender Shades
strings.timeline.t7.text: With Timnit Gebru, publishes an intersectional error study at FAT*, evaluating three commercial gender classifiers of that period.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Founds the Algorithmic Justice League
strings.timeline.t8.text: Creates an organization combining research, art and advocacy around AI bias and participation by affected communities.
